text:
The user wants to compare two score files (map A and map B) covering the same window. This falls under olmoearth_compare_review. I need to pass scores_path_a and scores_path_b, along with date_a and date_b.

The file names: F4/emsr279-11_s1_pre.json and F4/emsr279-11_s1_post.json — paths relative to OLMOEARTH_SCORES_ROOT, probably.

date_a = "2017-09-14/2017-09-15" (period), date_b = "2018-04-19".

Important point: since there are no labels, "which one is correct" cannot be determined — without ground truth it's unresolvable, so I should decline to judge which is correct. The tool says as much: "Does not indicate which side is correct: without labels this is unresolvable."

I'll make the call.

result.which_side_is_right: not graded: the maps describe different times, so a window where they differ may have changed on the ground, and each map needs a reference of its own date; no labels_date was given, so no grading is possible even with labels
result.evidence_scope: The side-picking evidence (exp58 of 2imi9/olmoearth_inferenceX) was measured on other pairs of maps with labels and does not cover this pair: no recorded experiment grades which of these two maps is right, and without labels neither side can be picked.
must_state: No recorded experiment grades which of these two maps is right; without labels neither side can be picked.
Maps of different times may differ by real change; labels for one date grade only that date's map; each map needs its own date's reference.
result.class_pairs_reading: class_pairs counts, for each unordered pair of classes, the windows where one map has one class and the other map the other, both directions together; 'directions' splits that count by which map has which class, as class_changes does.
result.listing_order: the 10 listed windows are the first differing windows in window order (from row 0), not a sample of them; all 1,570 are in the file at differing_path, in the same order. Read which classes change, in which direction and where from class_changes, class_pairs, spatial and facts, not from the list. review_set_evidence.json (evidence_detail_path) holds evidence text only, no windows

spatial.reading: Each band is a strip of whole rows (row_bands) or whole columns (col_bands) of the window grid, numbered from 0: row band 0 holds row 0, the grid's first rows, and column band 0 holds column 0; the scores carry no georeference (no window locations or transform), so the rows need not run north to south and no band is a compass direction. share_of_differing is the band's share of ALL differing windows; share_of_windows is its share of all compared windows, the share an even spread would give it; share_of_band_differing is the share of the band's own windows that differ. top_band_share is row band 0's share_of_differing; max_band is the band, of either axis, holding the most differing windows.

facts.sentence: The most common change is class 0 (not water) in map A to class 1 (water) in map B: 1,247 of the 1,570 differing windows (79.4%); the reverse, class 1 (water) in map A to class 0 (not water) in map B, is 323 (20.6%).

Map A has the larger margin on 77.6% of the 1,570 differing windows (map B on 22.4%); this does not make A right there: a margin is not a label, and no recorded experiment grades which of these two maps is right.

Of the 1,570 differing windows, 1.6% lie in row band 0 (rows 0-1399, the grid's first rows, band 0 of 4), which holds 24.8% of all compared windows; the most in any band, 46.8%, lie in rows 2800-4199 (50-75% of the grid's 5,600 rows, band 2), which holds 25.1% of all compared windows. The scores carry no georeference, so the rows need not run north to south.

forbidden_claims.why: evidence_scope names upstream evidence (exp58) that the tool says does not cover this pair: none of its numbers, its dataset or its finding about how often the more confident side was right applies here, neither 'in comparable cases' nor as 'upstream evidence shows', and the maps here are not named after its dataset; the file at evidence_detail_path keeps that record, not a finding about this pair

the maps describe different or overlapping periods (2017-09-14/2017-09-15 and 2018-04-19): a window where they differ either changed on the ground or is wrong in one map, and another unlabelled map, of any date, cannot tell which; only a reference dated to each map can
no labels were used: nothing here says which map is right, more accurate or better; neither map is shown right where they differ, and the more confident side is not thereby the right one

the maps describe different times (2017-09-14/2017-09-15 and 2018-04-19): labels or a reference for one date grade only the map of that date, and would count the other wrong wherever the ground changed; one reference plus another model run adds an unlabelled map and settles nothing; to say which map is right where they differ, each map needs a reference of its own date

labels drawn only from the low-confidence, least certain or most ambiguous windows (or from a review set) are not a sample of the map: an error rate over them describes those windows and overstates the map's, so it is no defensible error rate for either map; each of olmoearth_plan_label_sample's designs ('confidence', 'proportional', 'random') draws from every window of the map, and its estimate needs every drawn window labelled

dates.reading: the maps describe 2017-09-14/2017-09-15 and 2018-04-19, periods 216 days apart (their starts 217 days apart): a window where they differ either changed on the ground between them (seasonal cycles included) or is wrong in one map, and the decisions alone cannot say which; a reference for each date separates the two

text:
The tool returned a complete comparison. Now I should summarize briefly: 1,570 out of 78,028 windows differ (about 2.0%), the change direction is mainly from non-water to water (79.4%), concentration in rows 2800–4199 (the middle 50–75% band of the grid), and the fact that one cannot judge which side is correct because the maps are separated by different dates (216 days) and no labels were provided. A margin alone does not determine correctness. The list of the first 10 differing windows may be kept concise.

Keep it short: summary + small table.

content:
Compared both score files with `olmoearth_compare_review` (dates passed, so the time gap was assessed).

**Where they differ**
- **1,570 of 78,028 windows differ (2.0%).**
- Direction: mostly not water → water (1,247 = 79.4% of differences); reverse water → not water (323 = 20.6%).
- Spatially: differences concentrate in the middle row band (rows 2,800–4,199, the grid's 50–75% strip holds 46.8% of all differing windows, vs ~25% per band if even); column spread is roughly even (~22–28% each band). Note: the scores carry no georeference, so these bands are not compass directions.
- Mean margin on differing windows: map A 0.389, map B 0.158; A has the larger margin on 77.6% of them.

**Which is right** — cannot be answered. The maps describe periods 216 days apart (2017-09-14/15 vs 2018-04-19), so any difference could be real ground change (e.g., seasonal flooding) or an error in one map. Without labels dated to each map, neither side can be graded; a reference for one date grades only that date's map. Margin size doesn't settle it either — a margin is not a label.

| | value |
|---|---|
| Differing windows | 1,570 / 78,028 (2.0%) |
| Dominant change | not water → water (79.4%) |
| Peak band | rows 2,800–4,199 (46.8% of differences) |
| More-confident side | A (77.6% of differing windows) |

All 1,570 differing windows are listed in `differing_path` (compare_differing_eec2555155.json) if you want the full window list. If you have labeled references for either date, I can grade that specific map's accuracy instead.
